Differential abundance between conditions

Source: R/quant-stats.R
test_differential.Rd

Fits a linear model per feature and tests every requested condition pair. With method = "limma" (default) the model is ~ 0 + Condition with pairwise contrasts and empirical-Bayes moderation (limma::eBayes(), trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE): with the 3–5 replicates typical of an immunopeptidomics experiment the per-feature variance estimate is extremely noisy, and shrinking it towards a mean-variance trend fitted across all features increases power and controls the FDR better than per-feature t-tests (Smyth 2004; Kammers et al. 2015). trend = TRUE accounts for the pronounced intensity-dependent variance of label-free MS, robust = TRUE keeps a few wildly variable features from inflating the prior variance (Phipson et al. 2016). limma fits each row on its observed values, so the matrix may (and by default does) contain NAs.

Usage

test_differential(
  mat,
  coldata,
  contrasts = NULL,
  method = c("limma", "ttest"),
  block = NULL,
  trend = TRUE,
  robust = TRUE,
  min_obs = 2
)

Arguments

mat

Numeric matrix of (normalized) log2 intensities.

coldata

Column metadata from build_quant_matrix() (Unit, Condition, BioReplicate).

contrasts

List of length-2 character vectors c(reference, test), as produced by utils::combn() on the condition levels. NULL (default) uses all pairwise comparisons in factor order.

method

"limma" (default) or "ttest".

block

Optional blocking variable (name of a coldata column, or a vector of length ncol(mat)) passed to limma::duplicateCorrelation() — e.g. "BioReplicate" when the columns are individual runs, or a patient identifier in a paired design. Ignored by method = "ttest".

trend, robust

Passed to limma::eBayes(). Defaults TRUE.

min_obs

Minimum quantified values required per group for a feature to be tested by method = "ttest". Default 2.

Value

A data frame with one row per feature and contrast: Contrast, Feature, logFC (positive = higher in the test condition), AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val (BH within contrast), B (limma only), n_obs_ref, n_obs_test. For method = "limma" the fitted MArrayLM object is attached as the attribute fit (used for the mean-variance diagnostic plot).

Details

method = "ttest" runs an ordinary Welch t-test per feature and contrast with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment — a dependency-free fallback and a useful sanity check against the moderated result.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- test_differential(mat_n, qm$coldata, method = "limma")
head(res[order(res$adj.P.Val), ])
} # }
